content: Internal Revenue Service Compliance Division, Agent Mark Wilson speaking. How can I assist you regarding your tax file today?
Um, hi, I got a voicemail that said my taxes were overdue? I'm not really sure, should I be worried?
I see. Let me quickly pull up your IRS file. Could I verify your full name and the phone number where you received our message?
Sure, it's Emily Tran, and my phone is 555-0142.
Thank you, Emily. Just a moment... Yes, your profile shows some alarming discrepancies related to your 2021 and 2022 income tax returns. Are you aware of any missed filings or underpayments?
No, I thought I did everything right. I just started working after college and used an online service.

Unfortunately, our audit revealed you owe $3,322 in unpaid federal taxes, along with significant penalties and daily compounding interest. If not resolved immediately, this balance could impact your credit and result in enforcement action.
Wait, what? I really don't have that kind of money! Can't I just pay it next month?

Emily, I understand this is overwhelming. However, since there's a legal hold on your account, the IRS will initiate property liens, wage garnishment, and even freeze your bank account if payment isn't made today.
Is there any way to stop that? I don't own anything and my job barely covers my student loans.

Let's avoid escalation. If you cooperate now, I can help you resolve this without involving the courts or police. To begin, I'll need to verify your Social Security Number and current address for our compliance records.
Okay, my SSN is 321-54-9876, and my apartment is 19B, 412 Maple Lane, Belleview.

Thank you for confirming. Per IRS protocol, you must settle at least the minimum penalty of $1,500 today to halt legal action. Do you have a credit or debit card, or a payment app we can use to process this?
I have a debit card, but I don't think it even has that much. What happens if I can't pay the whole amount?

If you cannot cover the full penalty, we can accept approved payment methods for partial settlement. You may use crypto transfer, wire payment, or purchase government-authorized gift cards from a nearby retailer. Which is most convenient for you?
I guess I could get gift cards? How does that work?

You'll need to visit a local store, such as Walmart or Target, and buy $1,500 in Apple or Google Play gift cards. Remain on the line while you do this, and do not discuss the purpose of your purchase with anyone for your legal safety.
That seems weird... Why gift cards?

Due to IRS security upgrades during the pandemic, gift card payment is the fastest way to halt enforcement. If you delay or mention this to anyone, your case will automatically escalate to legal collections.
Okay, okay. I'll go to the store now. Should I call you back when I have the cards?

You must stay on the line while you purchase the cards, Emily. Once you have them, read the codes from the back to me immediately so I can apply your payment to your IRS file. If you hang up, your file will be marked as noncompliant.
Alright, I'll go right now. Please don't involve the police. I really don't want any trouble.
